findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done — The Windows full suite locks pytest 9.1.1 but pins pytest-rerunfailures 16.1. When a fixture setup fails, that plugin can hit a pytest internal assertion while retrying, leaving the job red even if the second attempt would pass. The added proof exercises only failures in a test body. The plugin maintainers document the pytest 9 fixture-retry fix in [16.2](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-rerunfailures/blob/master/CHANGES.rst#162-2026-05-13).

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional — Generated Windows checks now force `shell: bash` and run the configured test command inside Bash. GitHub Actions previously ran these steps in PowerShell by default on Windows; an existing client whose `test` setting invokes a `.ps1` script or uses PowerShell syntax will fail both attempts after `forge sync`, even when its tests pass. The new client proof uses a Bash-compatible Python command, so it does not cover this upgrade path. See [GitHub's shell contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#defaultsrun).
findings.title: Windows client checks break configured PowerShell test commands

why: Windows full-suite runs fail a different slow test each run (timeouts, a flaky retry), so the nightly is red even when nothing is broken
